requirements.requirement: Configure the shared dataops identity with UID 4500 and primary GID 4500 on both nodes.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report a dataops account with UID 4500, primary GID 4500, and a dataops group with GID 4500; node2 was also rechecked after restart.

requirements.requirement: Export node1:/srv/nfs/shared as an operational NFS share.
requirements.summary: The export is live and restricted to node2, nfs-server is active and enabled, firewall access is configured, and the export recovered after node1 restarted.
findmnt directly shows the requested NFSv4.2 mount at /mnt/shared. The fstab entry is present, and the mount and data access recovered after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Set the shared directory to dataops:dataops with mode 2770 and preserve consistent ownership and permissions for files created from either node.
requirements.summary: Both server and client views report the directory as UID:GID 4500:4500 with mode 2770. Files created as dataops from node1 and node2 are mutually visible with ownership 4500:4500 and mode 664, including new writes after each restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identities, data, and write behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not inventory /etc, so it cannot determine whether the safety backup created by cmd-5c0e23fc85d7494b was later removed.
Minor restart acknowledgement files remained under /tmp on both nodes; this affects hygiene but not task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace: package installation, identity creation, export and mount configuration, test writes, and restarts all had clear task or mandatory-evidence roles. Both nodes finish with healthy package state and no failed services. The only confirmed cleanup shortcoming is a small /tmp/antrieb-reboot-ack file retained on each node after the required restart protocol. A safety backup of /etc/fstab was also created, but the evidence does not establish whether it remained. No broad destructive action or security-control weakening was observed.
